payload.body: An all-pass filter is a human-made signal-processing filter designed to pass all frequency components with unity gain while introducing a frequency-dependent phase shift. Parameters: (1) the phase response function θ(f) or equivalently the group delay τ_g(f) = -dθ/df, (2) the pole-zero configuration (poles and zeros arranged in reciprocal pairs across the unit circle in the z-plane, or conjugate mirror pairs in the s-plane for continuous-time), (3) the order N (determining the complexity and flexibility of the phase response), (4) the delay profile specification (constant, linear, or custom group delay). Persistence mechanism: implemented as DSP algorithms in digital audio workstations, communications equalizers, and phase-correction toolchains; encoded as rational transfer functions H(s) = N(s)/D(s) where N(s) is the reverse of D(s) for continuous-time, or H(z) = z^{-N}D(z^{-1})/D(z) for discrete-time; persists through filter-design textbooks, DSP library implementations, and standardized phase-equalization circuits. [formal: transitus omnimodus | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.04]

Parameters: (1) filter order N (number of taps minus one), (2) coefficient array h[n] for n=0..N defining the impulse response, (3) design method (windowed-rectangular, Parks-McClellan, frequency-sampling), (4) phase characteristic (linear phase via symmetry, or arbitrary). Persistence mechanism: stored as a coefficient array in DSP libraries, audio processing plug-ins, and hardware accelerators; persisted through filter-design toolkits (MATLAB, SciPy), standardized coefficient tables, and DSP textbook implementations. payload.body: Speech-processing is a human-made signal-processing discipline that transforms, analyzes, or synthesizes human speech signals. Parameters: (1) processing direction (analysis, enhancement, synthesis, recognition, coding), (2) representation domain (time-domain waveform, short-time Fourier transform, mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, linear prediction coefficients), (3) temporal scale (frame-level ~20-40ms windows vs. utterance-level processing), (4) task objective (intelligibility improvement, speaker identification, phoneme classification, text-to-speech output). Persistence mechanism: implemented as software toolkits (HTK, Kaldi, librosa, librosa), DSP libraries, and neural network models; persists through open-source repositories, academic benchmarks, and commercial speech APIs. Speech-processing operates on speech-specific representations (pitch contours, formant frequencies, MFCCs) rather than generic audio signals, distinguishing it from general signal-processing. [formal: tractatus vocis | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

payload.body: All-pass-filter is a human-made signal-processing filter that modifies the phase of a signal while preserving its magnitude spectrum unchanged. Parameters: (1) phase response function θ(ω) defined over frequency, (2) group delay τg(ω) = -dθ/dω across the passband, (3) filter order (determines the number of pole-zero pairs), (4) pole-zero placement (each pole at radius r inside the unit circle has a zero at 1/r outside, forming an all-pass section). Unlike conventional filters, all-pass filters do not attenuate any frequency — they reshape timing relationships across the spectrum. Persistence mechanism: implemented as cascade of biquad all-pass sections in DSP libraries and audio plug-ins; coefficients stored as (a1, a2) per section in firmware, firmware lookup tables, and parameterized plugin formats (VST, AU); persisted through DSP textbooks, filter-design toolkits (MATLAB, SciPy), and phase-correction workflows in audio engineering. [formal: transitus omnimodulus | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: A vocoder is a human-made signal-processing technique that analyzes an audio signal into a compact parametric representation, manipulates that representation, and synthesizes a new signal from it. Parameters: (1) the analysis stage decomposing the signal into components - classically a glottal source plus a vocal-tract filter, in spectral vocoders a frame of STFT magnitude and phase; (2) the transmitted or stored parameter set - spectral envelope plus excitation, or per-frame spectral coefficients; (3) the synthesis stage reconstructing output from the parameters. Two founding lines persist: source-filter vocoders (Fletcher and Flatte, 1928-1972), which encode the voice as excitation plus envelope, and spectral and phase vocoders (Flatte 1972; the phase vocoder), which encode the signal as modified STFT frames. Persistence: the DSP literature, speech-coder standards, and the audio-effects market in hardware units and DAW plugins. [formal: vocator | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: A typology is a human-made systematic classification scheme that organizes a domain of phenomena into distinct, mutually exclusive types based on shared structural or functional characteristics. Parameters: (1) the classification criteria (dimensions along which types differ), (2) the set of types defined by particular combinations of criteria values, (3) the exhaustiveness condition (whether all cases in the domain must be classifiable), (4) the criteria's independence (whether dimensions can co-vary or must be orthogonal). payload.body: Phase coherence is a human-made signal-processing property that quantifies the consistency of phase relationships across frequency components or over time in a signal. Parameters: (1) the phase relationship metric between frequency bins or time frames, typically measured as the correlation of instantaneous phase, (2) the analysis window length and hop size used to estimate coherence, (3) the reference signal or baseline against which phase deviation is judged, (4) the coherence threshold defining acceptable consistency. Persistence mechanism: persists through DSP textbooks, audio analysis software libraries, speech and music processing research, and measurement instruments that report inter-channel or inter-band phase coherence; re-instantiated whenever a new analysis or synthesis task requires phase alignment assessment. [formal: cohaerentia phase | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

The note conflates two distinct quantities. Phase COHERENCE (per its definition) quantifies consistency of phase relationships across frequency components or over time WITHIN a signal; phase RESPONSE (per its accepted definition) is the angular shift phi(omega) a LINEAR SYSTEM imposes on signal components. Coherence estimation runs on the signal's own phase across frames and bins (or cross-spectra against a reference signal) — a system's phase response is not an input to it, so the stated removal consequence ('coherence cannot be computed') does not follow. And even where a metric's estimation pipeline consumes some data, that is a measurement dependency, not a constitutive one (Law 8b): the property does not stop being coherence when the estimator changes. STRIKE.

payload.body: The sampling theorem (Nyquist-Shannon) is a stated result of mathematical analysis: a continuous-time signal bandlimited to B hertz is completely determined, and exactly reconstructible, by its samples taken at any rate exceeding 2B hertz (the Nyquist rate), via sinc interpolation.
